title: House of compassion
hook: karunaalay hain: He is the home of compassion (Jaap, harbolmana)

segments.voice: Yesterday, ender and sustainer of all, sarab kaal, sarab paal, and your line, ends and keeps. Did an ending show you what it was feeding? Today, a new quick meter, and a house. Day three hundred forty-nine.

Everybody has, or wishes they had, one kitchen like this. A grandmother's, an aunt's, a friend's mom's. You could show up unannounced, any hour, after any kind of day, and the kettle went on before you'd finished saying hello. Nobody asked what you'd done wrong. Nobody made you earn the chair. You just came in, and you were cared for, because that's what the house was for. Some people are kind now and then. Some people are a place you can go. Jaap Sahib names the One like that second kind. Today: house of compassion.
screen: `ONE KITCHEN YOU COULD ALWAYS GO TO.` → `THE KETTLE WENT ON BEFORE HELLO.` → `SOME PEOPLE ARE A PLACE.`

segments.voice: Jaap shifts into yet another meter, harbolmana, with tiny, fast lines of just two words each, and the first of them is karunaalay hain. It's two words fused. Karunaa is compassion, the feeling that moves toward someone's suffering. Aalay, from aalaya, is a dwelling, a home. You know that second word already, hidden in a mountain range: Himalaya is hima, snow, plus aalaya, home. The home of snow. So karunaalay is the home of compassion. You are the house where compassion lives. That's a different picture from compassionate. A compassionate person feels it sometimes, in a good mood, on a good day. A home of compassion is where it lives all the time, whether anyone visits or not. It's the kitchen where the kettle is always ready. Sikhs have a word close to karunaa that they use for a human virtue: daya, kindness, mercy. It's often listed among the virtues a Sikh tries to grow, with truth, contentment, humility and love. And Guru Nanak gives daya a startling job. In Japji, he takes the old myth of a bull holding the earth on its back and says: the bull is dharma, righteousness, and dharma is the child of daya, of compassion. Compassion, in other words, is what holds the world up. So when Jaap calls the One the house of compassion, it's also hinting at what a Sikh home and a Sikh heart might try to be. Not kind sometimes. A place people can come.
screen: `HARBOLMANA: TWO QUICK WORDS A LINE.` · `KARUNAA: COMPASSION. AALAY: HOME.` · `NOT KIND SOMETIMES: A PLACE TO COME.` · `DAYA: THE CHILD WHO HOLDS UP THE WORLD.` · then, large: `HOME OF COMPASSION.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: be a home of compassion once. Think of someone who might need a place to land right now: a friend going through something, a coworker who's struggling, a relative who's lonely. Picture them walking into a warm kitchen, and picture yourself putting the kettle on. Breathe slowly. Then decide one small way to be that place for them today: a message, a call, a door left open. If you pray, you can say karunaalay hain. The bell holds the time.
Karunaa. Compassion, the feeling that moves toward suffering; and in Jaap, karunaalay, the One as the home where compassion always lives.
Your line: home of compassion. Today, be the kitchen someone can walk into: open your door, your phone, or your attention to one person who needs it. Day three hundred forty-nine.

howItsDone: Sikhs recite the quick harbolmana lines of Jaap Sahib each morning, and daya, compassion, is taught as one of the core virtues alongside truth, contentment, humility and love.

the bull that holds up the earth is dharma, born of daya.

fork.setup: the old myth says a bull holds the earth on its back. what does Guru Nanak say the bull really is?
fork.reveal: in Japji, the bull is dharma, and dharma is the child of daya: compassion is what holds the world up.

original.note: Gurmukhi: karunaa, compassion; Jaap's karunaalay is its home.

trapdoor: what you thought: house of compassion is a pretty way of saying kind.
what it means: the One is where compassion lives all the time, a place anyone can come to.
what a scholar hears: karunaalay is karuna + alaya (as in Himalaya, hima + alaya), opening the harbolmana chhand; Japji 16 makes dharma the son of daya.

sources.ref: Jaap Sahib, harbolmana chhand: karunaalay hain
Japji, pauri 16: dharma, the son of compassion (daya)

notes: Harbolmana stanza opening 'karunaalay hain, ar ghaalay hain, khal khanddan hain, mahi manddan hain': confirm; only karunaalay is taught today, khal khanddan is tomorrow.
Karunaalay = karuna + alaya; Himalaya = hima + alaya: standard, confirm.
Five virtues list (sat, santokh, daya, nimrata, pyaar) is a common modern teaching list; phrased 'often listed'. Confirm.
Japji pauri 16 'dhaul dharam daya ka poot', paraphrased; confirm.
